primary_diagnosis_treated: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease (post‑NSTEMI) with uncontrolled dyslipidaemia
nice_guideline_used: NICE CG126 / NG185 (secondary prevention after ACS) and NICE NG106 (heart failure considerations)

medications.duration: Lifelong – review annually and after any dose change
medications.purpose: Blood pressure control and cardioprotection after MI
medications.nice_justification: CG126 recommends ACE‑I for all IHD patients, especially with hypertension or LV dysfunction (CG126, §1.2).

medications.duration: Lifelong – review annually, titrate to HR 55‑60 bpm
medications.purpose: Post‑MI beta‑blockade for mortality reduction and symptom control
medications.nice_justification: CG126 recommends beta‑blocker as first‑line anti‑anginal and secondary‑prevention after MI (CG126, §1.3).
CG126 advises lifelong low‑dose aspirin for all patients with established coronary artery disease (CG126, §1.1).

medications.duration: 12 months from date of NSTEMI (if within 12 months; thereafter consider de‑escalation to clopidogrel)
medications.nice_justification: CG126 recommends 12 months of DAPT with aspirin + prasugrel after ACS when no contraindication (CG126, §1.1).

medications.duration: Lifelong – review lipid profile at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Intensive LDL‑C lowering for secondary prevention
medications.nice_justification: CG126 advises high‑intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg) for all patients with established CVD to achieve >40 % reduction in non‑HDL cholesterol (CG126, §1.4).

medications.duration: Until LDL‑C <1.8 mmol/L (≈70 mg/dL), then review
medications.purpose: Add‑on therapy if LDL‑C remains >1.8 mmol/L after 4‑6 weeks of maximised statin
medications.nice_justification: CG126 permits ezetimibe as add‑on when LDL‑C target not met on high‑intensity statin (CG126, §1.4).

medications.dose: 1 g orally every 6‑8 hours (max 4 g/24 h)
medications.purpose: Pain relief for knee osteoarthritis while avoiding NSAID‑related renal/CV risk
medications.nice_justification: NG106 advises avoidance of systemic NSAIDs in HF/CVD patients; paracetamol is the recommended alternative (NG106, §2.2).

medications.purpose: Add‑on antihypertensive if target BP not achieved on ACE‑I alone
medications.nice_justification: NG136 recommends adding a thiazide‑like diuretic for hypertension when ACE‑I monotherapy is insufficient (NG136, §2.1).

interactions_checked.interaction: Increased risk of acute kidney injury, hyperkalaemia and reduced antihypertensive effect
interactions_checked.action: Discontinue naproxen; monitor renal function and electrolytes after stopping NSAID

interactions_checked.interaction: Duplicate ACE‑inhibitor therapy – excess risk of hypotension, renal impairment and hyperkalaemia
Intended dual antiplatelet therapy; synergistic effect required for post‑ACS management

contraindications.reason: Contra‑indicated in patients with cardiovascular disease, hypertension and possible chronic kidney disease; increases risk of fluid retention and renal impairment (NG106, NG185).
contraindications.alternative: Paracetamol 1 g q6‑8 h PRN or topical NSAID gel

contraindications.reason: Duplicate ACE‑inhibitor therapy is unsafe and not recommended; increases risk of hypotension and renal dysfunction.

treatment_summary: The plan optimises secondary‑prevention after NSTEMI by consolidating ACE‑inhibitor therapy (keep lisinopril, stop enalapril), maintaining beta‑blockade, prescribing lifelong high‑intensity atorvastatin, and adding ezetimibe if LDL‑C remains >1.8 mmol/L. Dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin + prasugrel is continued for the recommended 12 months. NSAID naproxen is stopped due to cardiovascular and renal risk and replaced with paracetamol. Indapamide is added only if blood pressure remains uncontrolled. All changes follow NICE CG126/NG185 for ACS and NG106 for heart‑failure‑related considerations, with monitoring of renal function, electrolytes, liver enzymes, lipids, and blood pressure as stipulated by the guidelines.
